source: Minchat Shai on Gen 42:6 (the precise books)
claim_en: am ('the PEOPLE of the land'): the precise books rule GALGAL (the wheel stroke) with NO maqqef; SNAPSHOT writes the munach (the upright conjunctive stroke) with no maqqef — wheel-class station TEN, the stream in the munach camp at all ten (maqqef-absence checked; the stroke asserted in-stream).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 42:4 (the Masorah's seventeen; the Ramah's seven)
claim_en: BINYAMIN ('Benjamin') written FULL — yod between the mem and the nun: the Ramah counts SEVEN such fulls in the Torah, and the census is EXACT: the naming (Gen 35:18), the guarding (42:4), the sending (43:14), the seeing (43:16), the greeting (43:29), the kissing (45:12), the blessing (49:27) — while the SAME chapter writes the demanded son LEAN (binyamin without yod, 42:36, asserted): full when held, lean when claimed.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 42:7 (the Hilleli and Yerushalmi copies; the Masorah's seventeen fulls)
claim_en: va-yitnaker ALEHEM ('he made himself strange TO THEM'): the Hilleli copy lean, the Yerushalmi and ALL precise books FULL (one of the Masorah's seventeen fulls) — SNAPSHOT full, the stream with the precise books AGAINST the Hilleli (the seesaw: with the Hilleli at the lean cows, against it here) — and the SAME VERSE writes its second to-them LEAN (alehem, idx 11), excluded from the count by the Masorah's own note (both tokens asserted; the full form checked via its yod).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 42:3 (the Aspamia codex; Rabbenu Gershom's book)
claim_en: lishbor bar MI-MITZRAYIM ('to buy grain FROM Egypt'): so write the Aspamia codex and Rabbenu Gershom's book, against copies that read be-mitzrayim ('in Egypt') — SNAPSHOT writes the from-form with the precise books.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 42:24 (the Masorah; Mikhlol; Shorashim)
claim_en: va-YEESOR oto ('and he BOUND him' — Simeon): the alef in CHATAF SEGOL — the Masorah's note: none other so SOFT; its file counts three bind-verbs of this shape — one soft (Simeon, here) and two HARD (alef in plain sheva): Joseph binding his chariot to meet his father (Gen 46:29) and Pharaoh binding his chariot to chase Israel (Exod 14:6). A brother bound softly; the chariots hard.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 42:29 (the Hilleli and Yerushalmi copies; the Ramah)
claim_en: va-YAGIDU lo ('and they TOLD him') FULL: the Hilleli copy alone lean; the Yerushalmi, every book, and the Masorah full — for the Ramah counts the Torah's LEAN tellings as exactly TWO: the well found (va-yagidu lean, Gen 26:32) and 'Joseph still lives' (Gen 45:26) — and the lean census verifies EXACT in-stream: the two lean tellings are a well and a lost son; every other telling keeps its yod.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 42:11 (the Masorah)
claim_en: NACHNU ('we', the clipped form without the alef): exactly TWICE in the Torah — the brothers' 'sons of one man are WE' and the Reubenites' war-pledge 'WE will cross armed' (Num 32:32); the Masorah's third is 'WE have transgressed' (Lam 3:42, named, Tanakh-side). The Kitzur reads the three as one speech — armed, and guilty; and hears the clipped letter as the missing brother.

SEVATI ('my gray hair') FULL with the yod: the Ramah rules every gray-hair form in the Torah full, and the file verifies EXACT — sevati twice (42:38 and 44:29), sevat once (44:31): all three are Jacob's hair, all three bound to a going-down-to-Sheol clause, all three full.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 42:36 (the Masorah)
claim_en: alai hayu KHULANA ('upon me are they ALL'): the bare all-of-them form stands ONCE in the Torah; the Masorah pairs it with 'and you surpass them ALL' (Prov 31:29, named): all the losses land on one man. Calneh of Babel (Gen 10:10) wears the skeleton only with its vav — collision framed, not claimed.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 42:37 (the Masorah)
claim_en: TAMIT ('you may KILL' — Reuben's two-sons pledge): ONCE in the Torah; the Masorah's pair is 'and a seduced one kills envy' (Prov, named); the reading tradition rides the two-sons clause into Datan and Aviram (named): the pledge the father refused, read forward into the sons' rebellion.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 42:8 (the Masorah)
claim_en: ve-hem lo HIKIRUHU ('and they did not RECOGNIZE him'): the form stands ONCE in the Torah; the Masorah's pair is Job's friends who 'did not recognize him' from afar (Job 2:12, named): there suffering hid a man past knowing; here elevation — the slave had become the governor.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 42:2/9/22/28/30/32/35/38 (the chapter's file); Chizkuni
claim_en: The chapter's pointing-and-spelling file: ba-MITZRAYIM (42:2) with the bet DAGESHED (checked); ve-nichye (42:2) with the yod in segol, meraglim (42:9) with the gimel dageshed in every token, be-amtachti (42:28) with the bet soft, tzerorot (42:35) first vav lean second vav full (the Ramah, against a scroll-tikkun's variant), u-qraahu (42:38) with the vav in shuruk (Chizkuni), halo (42:22) full — all asserted; named: the lengthening stroke on ka-meraglim (42:30), the tevir file at asar anachnu (42:32), merikim with no paseq (42:35), and the Mikketz portion's no-break run (42:37-38).

va-yishtachavu-LO ('and they bowed TO HIM'): the bow-verb JOINED to its him-word by maqqef in-stream (checked) — and the Kitzur counts the joined phrase's letters: 'HERE THE DREAM WAS FULFILLED' (named): the letter's own receipt hung on the verse where gen_60's sheaves land.
